primitives.name: Top-K HNSW Retrieval
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Retrieval is top-k over an HNSW index.** No full-corpus scan, ever.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'q': 'query vector, dimensionless', 'k': 'number of retrieved premises, integer', '\\mathcal{R}': 'retrieved set of premises, set', '\\mathcal{P}': 'premise corpus, set'}
primitives.assumptions: Embeddings are normalized; HNSW index supports approximate nearest neighbor search.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Full-corpus scan fails due to O(N) complexity; HNSW maintains O(log N) query time.

layer2.mapping: The retrieval operator maps query vectors to premise sets via embedding similarity, aligning with GSE's situational trace update mechanism.

primitives.name: Activation Record Influence
primitives.verbatim_quote: **A premise influences a decision only through an activation record.** `lit.activation` is the only route; there is no other write path.
primitives.latex: \mathcal{A}(p, t) = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{if } p \text{ is activated at time } t \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
primitives.assumptions: Premise activation is deterministic given query and threshold.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Inference bypasses direct premise access; only activation records are used.

layer2.mapping: Activation records form a kernel for influence propagation in GSE's decision graph.
layer2.telemetry: Number of activated premises per signal.

primitives.name: Residual Feedback Mechanism
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Residual feedback is written by settlement, never by the scorer.** `lit.residual` is written by `applyResidualFeedback` (`packages/prediction-engine/src/literature/literature-retrieval.ts`), called from the settlement path.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\mathcal{F}_{\\text{residual}}': 'residual feedback, scalar', 's': 'signal, dimensionless', 'a': 'activation, scalar', '\\hat{y}_s': 'predicted outcome, scalar', 'y_s': 'actual outcome, scalar', '\\mathcal{L}': 'loss function, scalar'}
primitives.assumptions: Feedback is applied post-settlement; loss is bounded.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Feedback loop decouples prediction from learning; prevents scorer interference.

layer2.mapping: Residual feedback mirrors reinforcement learning updates in GSE's iterative refinement.
layer2.telemetry: Frequency and magnitude of residual feedback entries.

reasoning_traces.think:
The event-driven retrieval system operates under a dual constraint: top-k HNSW retrieval ensures efficient query resolution while activation records enforce causal consistency. The system's architecture is defined by four core laws: retrieval is constrained to HNSW indices, premises only influence decisions through activation records, feedback is exclusively written during settlement, and do-calculus applies only to promoted edges. These laws define a closed-loop system where each signal generates a retrieval trace, which is then processed through a causal graph. The failure contract ensures non-blocking behavior, and idempotency via event keys prevents redundant processing. The retrieval trace is updated iteratively through residual feedback, maintaining a stable yet adaptive knowledge base. The system's robustness stems from its reliance on structured data paths and explicit causality enforcement.
